channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Vannacci, Italy’s Rising Right-Wing Star, Has Yet to Meet Meloni
item.description: Italy’s Roberto Vannacci, the insurgent ultranationalist, has yet to meet Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni or have contact with her circle, as his rise begins to reshape her right-wing alliance before next year’s election.
item.dc:creator: Donato Paolo Mancini and Chiara Albanese

item.title: Portugal Sees No Threat to Schengen From Ceuta Migrant Surge
item.description: A surge of migrants into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta this summer didn’t pose a threat to the European Union’s free-travel zone, Portugal’s foreign minister said on Saturday.
item.dc:creator: Donato Paolo Mancini and Tiago Ramos Alfaro

item.title: Spotify’s Lorentzon Says He’d Leave Sweden If Wealth Tax Imposed
item.description: Spotify Technology SA co-founder Martin Lorentzon said he would leave Sweden immediately if the country introduces new wealth taxes, escalating concerns that proposals being debated ahead of this month’s election could drive entrepreneurs and capital abroad.
item.dc:creator: Rafaela Lindeberg

item.title: Trump’s Embrace of AI Data Centers Adds to GOP’s Midterm Peril
item.description: President Donald Trump’s fervent support for artificial intelligence data centers has put him at odds with voters who increasingly oppose them and comes despite direct warnings that his stance threatens to deepen Republicans’ peril in the November midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Courtney Subramanian, Jennifer A. Dlouhy and Steven T. Dennis

item.title: US Strikes 3 Iranian Tankers in Retaliation for IRGC Attacks
item.description: The US military said it launched strikes against three Iranian crude oil tankers in retaliation for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps targeting two US Navy warships with ballistic missiles.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Whitelaw

item.title: German Police Secure Explosive Devices Targeting Power Grid
item.description: Police in Germany discovered 12 explosive devices near overhead power lines in two districts in the country’s east, the latest in a spate of incidents targeting the country’s electricity infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: Christina Kyriasoglou and Eva Brendel

item.title: Trump Oil Deal Blindsides US Energy Companies
item.description: US oil executives say they were blindsided by the Trump administration’s Venezuela deal, which gives North American Blue Energy Partners access to fields that other companies had been pursuing. Bloomberg News White House Reporter Jennifer Dlouhy and Wall Street Journal National Security Reporter Vera Bergengruen are on Bloomberg This Weekend and say industry figures are also questioning whether the company can quickly develop new production and whether the arrangement can deliver lower gasoline prices before the midterm elections. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Putin Orders No Airstrikes on Kyiv While US Envoys Visit
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin has ordered Kremlin troops not to fire on Kyiv for three days as US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner prepare to visit, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Interfax.
item.dc:creator: Ros Krasny

item.title: Russia Pausing Kyiv Strikes as US Envoys Start Talks in Moscow
item.description: President Vladimir Putin ordered Russian forces to pause airstrikes on Kyiv as US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived for talks in Moscow with the Russian leader and other officials and prepared to travel on to the Ukrainian capital for the first time.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Kyiv Adapts to Constant Attack by Russian Jet-Powered Drones
item.description: As a resident of Boryspil, a satellite town of Kyiv, Kostyantyn Kuts has grown accustomed to regular night-time air raids. This past week has been different.
item.dc:creator: Volodymyr Verbianyi and Olesia Safronova

item.title: ‘We Can Only Win’: The Rise of the Far Right in Eastern Germany
item.description: In a village on the edge of Germany’s Harz mountains, families gathering at a beer-and-bratwurst summer picnic lined up for autographs and selfies from the man they want to lead the country’s first far-right state government since World War II.
item.dc:creator: Kamil Kowalcze

item.title: Burnham Gets His Own Breathing Space as Turmoil Engulfs Farage
item.description: Andy Burnham was just starting to face awkward questions about his plans as Britain’s prime minster this week. Instead, his biggest rival, Nigel Farage, ended up being the one under greater pressure to explain.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham

item.title: Tetris Distances Itself From White House’s Wall-Building Game
item.description: The maker of Tetris criticized a new White House digital game that mimics its classic puzzle by having players build a wall to stop migrants from crossing the US border.
item.dc:creator: María Paula Mijares Torres

item.title: Trump Demands Rate Cut After Jobs Report
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Larry Sabato, founder and director of the University of Virginia Center for Politics, says next week's Republican midterm convention, headlined by President Trump, is unlikely to reshape the dynamics of competitive House races. Rep. Greg Casar, chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, discusses legislation he is proposing with Sen. Bernie Sanders that would permanently ban artificial superintelligence, temporarily pause advanced AI development, and establish a new federal AI regulator. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Casar: US Needs to Put the Brakes on Advanced AI
item.description: Rep. Greg Casar, chair of the Congressional Progressive Caucus, discusses legislation he is proposing with Sen. Bernie Sanders that would permanently ban artificial superintelligence, temporarily pause advanced AI development, and establish a new federal AI regulator. Casar says companies should be barred from pursuing artificial superintelligence, while research on AI that is safe and beneficial could continue. He also discusses divisions among House Democrats and the role of the Progressive Caucus if Democrats win control of the chamber. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Sabato: RNC Convention Unlikely to Move Midterm Needle
item.description: Larry Sabato, founder and director of the University of Virginia Center for Politics, says next week's Republican midterm convention, headlined by President Trump, is unlikely to reshape the dynamics of competitive House races. He also discusses the legal fight over Missouri's congressional map and the dispute over mail ballots in North Carolina. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Judge Blocks Mail Ballot Change as Supreme Court Weighs Case
item.description: A federal judge has blocked the Postal Service from enforcing new limits on mail-in voting through the Nov. 3 midterm elections, extending a short-term pause as North Carolina began sending ballots on Friday and the US Justice Department was urging the Supreme Court to intervene.
item.dc:creator: Zoe Tillman and Brian Dowling

item.title: Trump’s Big Venezuela Deal Leaves US Oil Industry Blindsided
item.description: President Donald Trump has boasted that his sweeping oil accord with Venezuela — effectively giving the US control over much of the nation’s crude wealth — is possibly “the greatest deal ever made.”
item.dc:creator: Jennifer A. Dlouhy, Kevin Crowley and David Wethe

item.title: Xi’s Personnel Reshuffle Picks Up Pace as New Faces Emerge
item.description: China has named a former vice finance minister as acting mayor of Shanghai, the latest in a string of appointments ahead of a key congress for the ruling Communist Party next year.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Greek Premier Plans Fresh Economic Support as Election Nears
item.description: Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis is about to unveil an economic support package aimed at alleviating a cost of living crisis as he lays out his broader economic agenda ahead of next year’s national elections.
item.dc:creator: Sotiris Nikas
